units.zh: 劉焉字君郎，江夏竟陵人也，漢魯恭王之後裔，章帝元和中徙封竟陵，支庶家焉。
units.en: Liu Yan, courtesy name Junlang, came from Jingling in Jiangxia. His line descended from Han Prince Gong of Lu; during Emperor Zhang’s Yuanhe reign the fief was reassigned to Jingling, where a younger branch of the house made its home.
units.literal: Liu Yan, courtesy name Junlang, was a man of Jingling in Jiangxia; he was a descendant of Prince Gong of Lu of the Han; in the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang his enfeoffment was transferred to Jingling, and a cadet branch of the family settled there.

units.zh: 焉少仕州郡，以宗室拜中郎，後以師祝公喪去官。
units.en: As a young man Liu Yan held posts in local government; his status as imperial clansman won him appointment as a gentleman of the palace. He later resigned to observe mourning for his teacher, Duke Zhu.
units.literal: In youth Yan served in prefecture and commandery offices; because of his imperial-clan status he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace, and later, on account of mourning for his teacher Duke Zhu, left office.

units.zh: 〈臣松之案：祝公，司徒祝恬也。〉
units.en: 〈Pei Songzhi remarks: “Duke Zhu was Zhu Tian, who served as minister of education.”〉
units.literal: 〈Pei Songzhi’s note: Duke Zhu was Zhu Tian, Minister of Education.〉

units.zh: 居陽城山，積學教授，舉賢良方正，闢司徒府，歷雒陽令、冀州刺史、南陽太守、宗正、太常。
units.en: He withdrew to Mount Yangcheng, where he studied deeply and taught. Recommended as a worthy and upright candidate, he entered the minister of education’s bureau and rose through Luoyang magistrate, inspector of Ji, grand administrator of Nanyang, director of the imperial clan, and grand master of ceremonies.
units.literal: He dwelt on Mount Yangcheng, amassed learning and taught students; he was recommended as worthy and good, upright and true; he was summoned to the Minister of Education’s office, and in succession served as magistrate of Luoyang, inspector of Ji Province, grand administrator of Nanyang, director of the imperial clan, and grand master of ceremonies.

units.zh: 焉睹靈帝政治衰缺，王室多故，乃建議言：「刺史、太守，貨賂為官，割剝百姓，以致離叛。
units.en: Seeing Emperor Ling’s government falter and the house of Han beset by crisis, Liu Yan proposed: “Prefectural inspectors and grand administrators are buying their posts; they bleed the people until the realm splinters into revolt.
units.literal: Yan saw that Emperor Ling’s governance was decaying and deficient and the royal house had many troubles; then he proposed, saying: “Inspectors and grand administrators have purchased office with bribes; they flay and strip the common people, thereby bringing about separation and rebellion.

units.zh: 可選清名重臣以為牧伯，鎮安方夏。」
units.en: Choose men of unimpeachable name and real weight as regional governors, and charge them with restoring calm across the land.”
units.literal: It is possible to select men of pure reputation and weighty rank to serve as regional shepherds and command them to pacify and quiet the four directions and the summer realm.”

units.zh: 焉內求交阯牧，欲避世難。
units.en: Behind the scenes he angled for the governorship of Jiaozhi, hoping to sit out the gathering storm.
units.literal: Yan inwardly sought appointment as governor of Jiaozhi, wishing to escape the troubles of the age.

units.zh: 議未即行，侍中廣漢董扶私謂焉曰：「京師將亂，益州分野有天子氣。」
units.en: Before the plan could take effect, Palace Attendant Dong Fu of Guanghan took him aside: “Luoyang is heading for turmoil, and the stars over Yizhou show the aura of an emperor.”
units.literal: The proposal had not yet been put into effect when Palace Attendant Dong Fu of Guanghan privately said to Yan: “The capital is about to be in chaos; in the astrological field of Yizhou there is the qi of the Son of Heaven.”

units.zh: 焉聞扶言，意更在益州。
units.en: Those words fixed his mind on Yizhou more firmly than ever.
units.literal: When Yan heard Fu’s words, his intentions turned still more toward Yizhou.

units.zh: 會益州刺史郤儉賦斂煩擾，謠言遠聞，儉，郤正祖也。
units.en: About then Yizhou Inspector Xi Jian was grinding the people with heavy levies until rumor of it spread far; Xi Jian was an ancestor of Xi Zheng.
units.literal: It happened that Inspector of Yizhou Xi Jian levied taxes in vexing and harassing fashion, and rumors were heard from afar; Jian was the ancestor of Xi Zheng.

units.zh: 而并州殺刺史張壹，涼州殺刺史耿鄙，焉謀得施。
units.en: When Bing Province slew Inspector Zhang Yi and Liang slew Inspector Geng Bi, Liu Yan’s scheme could finally move forward.
units.literal: Meanwhile Bing Province killed Inspector Zhang Yi, and Liang Province killed Inspector Geng Bi; Yan’s plan could be carried out.

units.zh: 出為監軍使者，領益州牧，封陽城侯，當收儉治罪；
units.en: He was sent out as supervisory army envoy with the governorship of Yizhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangcheng, and charged to seize Xi Jian and bring him to justice;
units.literal: He went out as supervisory army envoy, took charge as governor of Yizhou, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangcheng, and was to arrest Jian and punish him according to law;

units.zh: 《續漢書》曰：是時用劉虞為幽州，劉焉為益州，劉表為荊州，賈琮為冀州。
units.en: The Continuation of the Book of Han records that Liu Yu was made governor of You, Liu Yan of Yizhou, Liu Biao of Jing, and Jia Cong of Ji.
units.literal: The Continuation of the Book of Han says: At this time Liu Yu was appointed to You Province, Liu Yan to Yizhou, Liu Biao to Jing Province, and Jia Cong to Ji Province.

units.zh: 虞等皆海內清名之士，或從列卿尚書以選為牧伯，各以本秩居任。
units.en: All were men of spotless reputation; some were promoted from the ranks of ministers and palace secretaries to provincial governorships while retaining their former titles.
units.literal: Yu and the others were all men of pure reputation within the realm; some were chosen as regional shepherds from among ranked ministers and masters of writing, each holding office at his original rank.

units.zh: 舊典：傳車參駕，施赤為帷裳。
units.en: By ancient custom they traveled in relay carriages with three teams and red drapery as their canopy.
units.literal: According to old precedent: relay carriages with three teams, red drapery used as curtains and canopies.

units.zh: 臣松之按：靈帝崩後，義軍起，孫堅殺荊州刺史王叡，然後劉表為荊州，不與焉同時也。
units.en: Pei Songzhi remarks: After Emperor Ling died and the loyalist armies rose, Sun Jian killed Jing inspector Wang Rui; Liu Biao’s appointment to Jing came only afterward and was not contemporaneous with Liu Yan’s.
units.literal: Your servant Songzhi notes: After Emperor Ling’s death righteous armies rose; Sun Jian killed Inspector of Jing Province Wang Rui, and only then was Liu Biao made governor of Jing—he was not appointed at the same time as Yan.

units.zh: 《漢靈帝紀》曰：帝引見焉，宣示方略，加以賞賜，敕焉為益州刺史。
units.en: The Annals of Emperor Ling record that the emperor received Liu Yan in audience, laid out his plans, rewarded him, and appointed him inspector of Yizhou.
units.literal: The Annals of Emperor Ling of Han say: The emperor summoned Yan for audience, displayed strategy and plans, bestowed rewards, and ordered Yan to be inspector of Yizhou.

units.zh: 前刺史劉雋、郤儉皆貪殘放濫，取受狼籍，元元無聊，呼嗟充野，焉到便收攝行法，以示萬姓，勿令漏露，使癰疽決潰，為國生梗。
units.en: His predecessors Liu Juan and Xi Jian had been rapacious and lawless, their extortion so rampant that the people were destitute and the countryside rang with lament. Yan was to arrest them at once, enforce the law before the people, and drain the abscess before it festered into a national crisis.
units.literal: The former inspectors Liu Juan and Xi Jian were both greedy, cruel, and unrestrained; their taking and receiving were in disorder; the common people were destitute; cries of lament filled the wilds. When Yan arrived he was to gather them in and enforce the law, to show the myriad people, not letting leaks appear, so that the abscess might burst and drain and not become a running sore for the state.

units.zh: 焉受命而行，以道路不通，住荊州東界。
units.en: Liu Yan set out on his commission but, with the roads blocked, halted on Jing Province’s eastern frontier.
units.literal: Yan received the command and set out; because the roads were impassable, he halted on the eastern border of Jing Province.

units.zh: 扶亦求為蜀郡西部屬國都尉，及太倉令
units.en: Dong Fu likewise sought appointment as commandant of the dependent state in western Shu Commandery.
units.literal: Dong Fu also requested appointment as commandant of the dependent state in the western part of Shu Commandery.

units.en: Some manuscripts insert “meeting” here.
units.literal: (hui “meeting” [variant])

units.zh: 巴西趙韙去官，俱隨焉。
units.en: Zhao Wei of Baxi, director of the Imperial Granary, resigned his post, and both men went with Liu Yan.
units.literal: Zhao Wei of Baxi, director of the Imperial Granary, left office, and both followed Yan.

units.zh: 陳壽《益部耆舊傳》曰：董扶字茂安。
units.en: Chen Shou’s Records of Elders of Yibu records: Dong Fu, courtesy name Mao’an.
units.literal: Chen Shou’s Records of Elders of Yibu says: Dong Fu, courtesy name Mao’an.

units.zh: 少從師學，兼通數經，善歐陽尚書，又事聘士楊厚，究極圖讖。
units.en: As a youth he studied under several masters, mastered multiple classics and Ouyang Gao’s version of the Book of Documents, and served the reclusive scholar Yang Hou in the study of prognostic charts.
units.literal: In youth he followed teachers in study, mastered several classics, excelled in Ouyang’s Book of Documents, and also served the reclusive scholar Yang Hou, thoroughly investigating charts and prognostications.

units.zh: 遂至京師，遊覽太學，還家講授，弟子自遠而至。
units.en: He went to the capital, studied at the Imperial Academy, then returned home to teach; students came from far and wide.
units.literal: Then he reached the capital, toured the Imperial Academy, returned home to lecture and teach, and disciples came from afar.

units.zh: 永康元年167年，日有蝕之，詔舉賢良方正之士，策問得失。
units.en: In 167, the first year of Yongkang, a solar eclipse prompted an edict summoning worthy and upright candidates for written policy examinations.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, 167, there was a solar eclipse; an edict summoned worthy and upright candidates, and policy questions were put on gains and losses.

units.zh: 左馮翊趙謙等舉扶，扶以病不詣，遙於長安上封事，遂稱疾篤歸家。
units.en: Zhao Qian of Zuofengyi and others recommended him, but Fu pleaded illness and stayed away, submitting a sealed memorial from Chang’an before declaring himself gravely ill and going home.
units.literal: Zuo Fengyi Zhao Qian and others recommended Fu; Fu, citing illness, did not go; from afar at Chang’an he submitted a sealed memorial, then claimed grave illness and returned home.

units.zh: 前後宰府十闢，公車三徵，再舉賢良方正、博士、有道皆不就，名稱尤重。
units.en: Provincial and central offices summoned him ten times, the imperial carriage three times, and he was twice recommended as worthy, erudite, and virtuous—yet he refused every call, and his fame only grew.
units.literal: Before and after, ten summonses came from chief ministers’ offices, three imperial carriage summonses, and twice he was recommended as worthy and upright, as erudite, and as possessing the Way—he accepted none; his reputation was especially weighty.

units.zh: 大將軍何進表薦扶曰：「資遊、夏之德，述孔氏之風，內懷焦、董消復之術。
units.en: Grand General He Jin memorialized in his favor: “He has the virtue of the ancient sages You and Xia, carries forward Confucius’s teaching, and holds within him the restorative arts of Jiao and Dong.
units.literal: Grand General He Jin memorialized recommending Fu, saying: “He possesses the virtue of You and Xia, expounds the style of the Kong clan, and inwardly holds the restorative arts of Jiao and Dong.

units.zh: 方今並、涼騷擾，西戎蠢叛，宜敕公車特召，待以異禮，諮謀奇策。」
units.en: With Bing and Liang in turmoil and the western tribes in revolt, the throne should summon him by imperial carriage with exceptional honors and seek his counsel on extraordinary measures.”
units.literal: Now Bing and Liang are in turmoil, the western Rong foolishly rebel; it is fitting to order the imperial carriage to summon him specially, treat him with exceptional ceremony, and consult him on extraordinary plans.”

units.zh: 於是靈帝徵扶，即拜侍中。
units.en: Emperor Ling then summoned Dong Fu and appointed him palace attendant on the spot.
units.literal: Thereupon Emperor Ling summoned Fu and immediately appointed him Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 在朝稱為儒宗，甚見器重。
units.en: At court he was hailed as the leading Confucian scholar and won deep respect.
units.literal: At court he was called the patriarch of scholars and was greatly valued and trusted.

units.zh: 求為蜀郡屬國都尉。
units.en: He asked for the post of commandant of Shu’s dependent state.
units.literal: He requested appointment as commandant of the dependent state in Shu Commandery.

units.zh: 扶出一歲而靈帝崩，天下大亂。
units.en: A year after he left the capital Emperor Ling died and the empire plunged into chaos.
units.literal: Fu had been out one year when Emperor Ling died and the realm fell into great chaos.

units.zh: 後去官，年八十二卒於家。
units.en: He later resigned and died at home at eighty-two.
units.literal: Later he left office; at age eighty-two he died at home.

units.zh: 始扶發辭抗論，益部少雙，故號曰
units.en: From the start his debating was unmatched in Yizhou, so he was nicknamed
units.literal: At first, when Fu began to speak in refutation and debate, few in Yibu could match him; therefore he was styled

units.zh: （致止）
units.en: Some manuscripts read “Zhizhi” (“he who stops”).
units.literal: (zhizhi “to stop” [variant])

units.zh: 至止，言人莫能當，所至而談止也。
units.en: “Zhizhi”—“the one who stops all talk”—for wherever he went debate fell silent.
units.literal: [Zhizhi “to the stop”], meaning no one could withstand him—wherever he went discussion ceased.

units.zh: 後丞相諸葛亮問秦宓以扶所長，宓曰：「董扶褒秋毫之善，貶纖芥之惡。」
units.en: Later Chancellor Zhuge Liang asked Qin Mi what Dong Fu excelled at. Mi replied: “Dong Fu praises goodness down to the finest hair and condemns wrongdoing down to the smallest flaw.”
units.literal: Later Chancellor Zhuge Liang asked Qin Mi about Fu’s strengths; Mi said: “Dong Fu praises the good even in an autumn down, and condemns evil even in a fiber of grass.”

units.zh: 是時益州逆賊馬相、趙祗等於綿竹縣自號黃巾，合聚疲役之民，一二日中得數千人，先殺綿竹令李升，吏民翕集，合萬餘人，便前破雒縣，攻益州殺儉，又到蜀郡、犍為，旬月之間，破壞三郡。
units.en: About then rebels Ma Xiang and Zhao Qi in Yizhou raised the Yellow Turban banner at Mianzhu, sweeping up worn-out conscripts. Within a day or two they had thousands of followers; they slew Magistrate Li Sheng, and officials and townsfolk rallied until their host passed ten thousand. They took Luoxian, struck down Inspector Xi Jian of Yizhou, then swept through Shu and Qianwei—three commanderies ruined inside a month.
units.literal: At this time [Yi] Province’s rebel bandits Ma Xiang, Zhao Qi, and others at Mianzhu County styled themselves Yellow Turbans; they gathered exhausted conscripted people; in one or two days they obtained several thousand men; first they killed Mianzhu magistrate Li Sheng; officials and common people flocked together, totaling more than ten thousand; then they advanced and broke Luoxian, attacked Yizhou and killed Jian, then went to Shu Commandery and Qianwei; within a month or so they destroyed three commanderies.

units.zh: 相自稱天子，眾以萬數。
units.en: Ma Xiang proclaimed himself emperor, and his following ran to tens of thousands.
units.literal: Xiang declared himself Son of Heaven; the multitude was counted in the tens of thousands.

units.zh: 州從事賈龍
units.en: The provincial clerk Jia Long
units.literal: Provincial clerk Jia Long

units.en: Alternate wording marks Jia Long as having long enjoyed local trust.
units.literal: (su ‘for a long time’ [variant])

units.zh: 領兵數百人在犍為東界，攝斂吏民，得千馀人，攻相等，數日破走，州界清靜。
units.en: He led a few hundred soldiers on Qianwei’s eastern march, rallied officials and townsfolk to more than a thousand, struck Ma Xiang’s host, and within days routed them; peace returned to the province.
units.literal: leading several hundred troops on the eastern border of Qianwei, gathered and collected officials and common people, obtained more than a thousand men, attacked Xiang and the others; in several days he broke them and drove them off; the borders of the province were quiet and pure.

units.zh: 龍乃選吏卒迎焉。
units.en: Jia Long then picked officers and troops to escort Liu Yan in.
units.literal: Long then selected clerks and soldiers to welcome Yan.

units.zh: 焉徙治綿竹，撫納離叛，務行寬惠，陰圖異計。
units.en: Liu Yan shifted his seat to Mianzhu, offering refuge to deserters and rebels while preaching mercy—yet all the while he nursed designs of his own.
units.literal: Yan moved his administration to Mianzhu, comforted and received those who had left or rebelled, strove to practice leniency and kindness, and secretly plotted unusual designs.

units.zh: 張魯母始以鬼道，又有少容，常往來焉家，故焉遣魯為督義司馬，住漢中，斷絕谷閣，殺害漢使。
units.en: Zhang Lu’s mother practiced spirit mediumship and still looked young; she was a frequent guest in Liu Yan’s house, so Yan appointed Zhang Lu marshal of righteous command and posted him in Hanzhong. Zhang Lu sealed the mountain defiles and murdered imperial messengers.
units.literal: Zhang Lu’s mother at first practiced the way of ghosts, and moreover had a youthful appearance; she constantly went back and forth to Yan’s household; therefore Yan dispatched Lu as marshal for supervising righteousness, stationed in Hanzhong, cut off the passes of the ravines, and killed Han envoys.

units.zh: 焉上書言米賊斷道，不得複通，又託他事殺州中豪強王咸、李權等十馀人，以立威刑。
units.en: Liu Yan memorialized that “rice-bandit” cultists had severed the roads and cut him off from court, then used other excuses to execute a dozen leading local families—Wang Xian and Li Quan among them—to cow the gentry.
units.literal: Yan submitted a memorial saying the rice bandits had cut the roads and he could not again communicate; moreover, under other pretexts he killed more than ten powerful magnates of the province such as Wang Xian and Li Quan, in order to establish awe-inspiring punishments.

units.zh: 〈《益部耆舊雜記》曰：李權字伯豫，為臨邛長。
units.en: 〈The Miscellaneous Records of the Elders of Yibu records: Li Quan, courtesy Boyu, served as magistrate of Linqiong.
units.literal: 〈The Miscellaneous Records of the Elders of Yibu says: Li Quan, courtesy name Boyu, was magistrate of Linqiong.

units.zh: 子福。
units.en: His son was named Fu.
units.literal: Son Fu.

units.zh: 見犍為楊戲《輔臣贊》。〉
units.en: See Yang Xi of Qianwei’s Encomia on Ministers.
units.literal: See Yang Xi of Qianwei’s Encomia on Ministers.

units.zh: 犍為太守任岐及賈龍由此反攻焉，焉擊殺岐、龍。
units.en: Ren Qi, grand administrator of Qianwei, and Jia Long then turned their arms on Liu Yan; Yan defeated them and put both men to death.
units.literal: Grand Administrator of Qianwei Ren Qi and Jia Long for this reason turned back and attacked Yan; Yan struck and killed Qi and Long.

units.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：劉焉起兵，不與天下討董卓，保州自守。
units.en: 〈The Record of Heroes states: Liu Yan mobilized his forces but refused to march with the coalition against Dong Zhuo, holding Yizhou for himself.
units.literal: 〈The Record of Heroes says: Liu Yan raised troops, did not join the realm in attacking Dong Zhuo, and protected the province to guard himself.

units.zh: 犍為太守任岐自稱將軍，與從事陳超舉兵擊焉，焉擊破之。
units.en: Ren Qi of Qianwei declared himself a general and, with Clerk Chen Chao, marched against Liu Yan; Yan shattered their army.
units.literal: Grand Administrator of Qianwei Ren Qi styled himself general; together with clerk Chen Chao he raised troops and struck Yan; Yan struck and broke them.

units.zh: 董卓使司徒趙謙將兵向州，說校尉賈龍，使引兵還擊焉，焉出青羌與戰，故能破殺。
units.en: Dong Zhuo dispatched Minister Zhao Qian against the province and won over Colonel Jia Long, turning him against Liu Yan. Yan answered with Qingqiang auxiliaries and so crushed the attack.
units.literal: Dong Zhuo sent Minister of Education Zhao Qian to lead troops toward the province, persuaded Colonel Jia Long, and made him lead troops back to attack Yan; Yan brought out Qingqiang and fought them, therefore was able to break and kill them.

units.zh: 岐、龍等皆蜀郡人。〉
units.en: Ren Qi, Jia Long, and their confederates were natives of Shu Commandery.
units.literal: Qi, Long, and the others were all men of Shu Commandery.

units.zh: 焉意漸盛，造作乘輿車具千馀乘。
units.en: Liu Yan’s ambitions swelled until he was building over a thousand sets of imperial carriage fittings.
units.literal: Yan’s intentions gradually grew great; he manufactured imperial carriage gear to the number of more than a thousand sets.

units.zh: 荊州牧劉表表上焉有似子夏在西河疑聖人之論。
units.en: Governor Liu Biao of Jing memorialized the throne, likening Liu Yan to Zixia west of the River—whose teaching had led men to doubt Confucius himself.
units.literal: Jing Province Governor Liu Biao memorialized upward that Yan had discourse resembling Zixia west of the He doubting the sage.

units.zh: 時焉子範為左中郎將，誕治書御史，璋為奉車都尉，皆從獻帝在長安，
units.en: His sons held court rank in Chang’an with Emperor Xian: Fan as left general of the gentlemen of the palace, Dan as imperial clerk censor, Zhang as commandant for the imperial chariot,
units.literal: At that time Yan’s son Fan was Left General of the Gentlemen of the Palace, Dan was imperial clerk censor, and Zhang was Commandant of the Chariots; all followed Emperor Xian at Chang’an,

units.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：範
units.en: 〈The Record of Heroes adds: Fan
units.literal: 〈The Record of Heroes says: Fan

units.en: One manuscript reads ‘heard’ here.
units.literal: (heard [variant])

units.zh: 父焉為益州牧，董卓所徵發，皆不至。
units.en: He learned that his father was governor of Yizhou and that none of Dong Zhuo’s summons had been obeyed.
units.literal: father Yan was governor of Yizhou; those whom Dong Zhuo summoned and drafted all did not arrive.

units.zh: 收范兄弟三人，鎖械於郿塢，為陰獄以系之。〉
units.en: Dong Zhuo clapped all three brothers in irons at the Mei bastion and locked them in a secret cell.
units.literal: He seized the three Fan brothers, shackled them at Mei’s bastion, and made a hidden prison to bind them.

units.zh: 惟
units.en: Only
units.literal: Only

units.en: Some texts read “younger” (son).
units.literal: (younger [variant])

units.zh: 子別部司馬瑁素隨焉。
units.en: The youngest, Mao, a major of a separate division, had stayed with his father in the west.
units.literal: son Separate-division Major Mao always followed Yan.

units.zh: 獻帝使璋曉諭焉，焉留璋不遣。
units.en: The emperor sent Liu Zhang west to reason with his father; Liu Yan kept him and never let him return.
units.literal: Emperor Xian sent Zhang to enlighten and instruct Yan; Yan detained Zhang and did not send him back.

units.zh: 〈《典略》曰：時璋為奉車都尉，在京師。
units.en: 〈The Compendium notes: Liu Zhang was then commandant for the chariot in Luoyang.
units.literal: 〈The Compendium says: at that time Zhang was Commandant of the Chariots, in the capital.

units.zh: 焉託疾召璋，璋自表省焉，焉遂留璋不還。〉
units.en: Liu Yan feigned illness to summon him; Zhang asked leave to visit his father—and never came back to court.
units.literal: Yan feigned illness and summoned Zhang; Zhang personally memorialized to visit Yan; Yan then detained Zhang and did not return him.

units.zh: 時征西將軍馬騰屯郿而反，焉及範與騰通謀，引兵襲長安。
units.en: When Ma Teng, general who conquers the west, rose in rebellion from his camp at Mei, Liu Yan and Liu Fan conspired with him to strike Chang’an.
units.literal: At that time General Who Conquers the West Ma Teng was stationed at Mei and rebelled; Yan and Fan communicated plots with Teng and led troops to raid Chang’an.

units.zh: 範謀洩，奔槐里，騰敗，退還涼州，範應時見殺，於是收誕行刑。
units.en: The plot unraveled: Fan fled to Huaili; Ma Teng was beaten back into Liangzhou; Fan was caught and killed, and Dan went to the executioner’s block.
units.literal: Fan’s plot leaked; he fled to Huaili; Teng was defeated, withdrew and returned to Liang Province; Fan in due course was seen and killed; thereupon Dan was seized and executed.

units.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：範從長安亡之馬騰營，從焉求兵。
units.en: 〈The Record of Heroes says: Fan slipped out of Chang’an to Ma Teng’s camp and begged his father for reinforcements.
units.literal: 〈The Record of Heroes says: Fan fled from Chang’an to Ma Teng’s camp and from Yan sought troops.

units.zh: 焉使校尉孫肇將兵往助之，敗於長安。〉
units.en: Liu Yan sent Colonel Sun Zhao with troops; they were routed before Chang’an.
units.literal: Yan ordered Colonel Sun Zhao to lead troops to go aid them; they were defeated at Chang’an.

units.zh: 議郎河南龐羲與焉通家，乃募將焉諸孫入蜀。
units.en: Pang Xi of Henan, a gentleman-adviser who was tied to the Liu family by marriage, raised men and shepherded Liu Yan’s grandsons to safety in Shu.
units.literal: Gentleman-adviser Pang Xi of Henan was connected by family with Yan; then he recruited and led Yan’s various grandsons into Shu.

units.zh: 時焉被天火燒城，車具蕩盡，延及民家。
units.en: Heaven-sent fire then consumed his city, devouring the carriage stockpiles and spreading into the commoners’ quarters.
units.literal: At that time Yan suffered heaven’s fire burning the city; carriage gear was completely swept away; it extended to common people’s homes.

units.zh: 焉徙治成都，既痛其子，又感祅災，興平元年，癰疽發背而卒。
units.en: He moved his government to Chengdu. Grief for his executed sons and shock at these portents broke him; in the first year of Xingping a carbuncle on his back killed him.
units.literal: Yan moved his administration to Chengdu; having already grieved for his sons, and moreover being moved by uncanny disasters, in the first year of Xingping, an abscess-boil erupted on his back and he died.

units.zh: 州大吏趙韙等貪璋溫仁，共上璋為益州刺史，詔書因以為監軍使者，領益州牧，以韙為征東中郎將，率眾擊劉表。
units.en: Senior officers led by Zhao Wei, liking Liu Zhang’s mild temper, jointly nominated him inspector of Yizhou. The court named him military overseer and governor of the province, appointed Zhao Wei general of the east who expands might, and ordered him to campaign against Liu Biao.
units.literal: Great clerks of the province such as Zhao Wei, coveting Zhang’s mild benevolence, jointly memorialized Zhang upward as inspector of Yizhou; an edict thereupon made him overseer of military affairs envoy, concurrently governor of Yizhou; Wei was made General of the East Who Expands Might, leading the host to attack Liu Biao.

units.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：焉死，子璋代為刺史。
units.en: 〈The Record of Heroes adds: When Liu Yan died, his son Liu Zhang succeeded as inspector.
units.literal: 〈The Record of Heroes says: when Yan died, his son Zhang replaced him as inspector.

units.zh: 會長安拜潁川扈瑁為刺史，入漢中。
units.en: Just then Chang’an named Hu Mao of Yingchuan inspector and sent him toward Hanzhong.
units.literal: It happened that Chang’an appointed Hu Mao of Yingchuan as inspector; he entered Hanzhong.

units.zh: 荊州別駕劉闔，璋將沈彌、婁發、甘寧反，擊璋不勝，走入荊州。
units.en: Liu He, chief clerk on Liu Biao’s staff, with Liu Zhang’s officers Shen Mi, Lou Fa, and Gan Ning rose against their master, failed, and bolted into Jingzhou.
units.literal: Jing Province chief clerk Liu He, Zhang’s generals Shen Mi, Lou Fa, and Gan Ning rebelled; they struck Zhang but did not win, and fled into Jing Province.

units.zh: 璋使趙韙進攻荊州，屯朐䏰。
units.en: Liu Zhang dispatched Zhao Wei against Jingzhou; he encamped at Quyi.
units.literal: Zhang sent Zhao Wei to advance and attack Jing Province, encamping at Quyi.

units.zh: 上蠢，下如振反。〉
units.en: Phonetic gloss for the toponym Quyi (first syllable as noted in the commentary; second like zhèn).
units.literal: Phonetic gloss for the toponym Quyi (first syllable as noted in the commentary; second like zhèn).

units.zh: 璋字季玉，既襲焉位，而張魯稍驕恣，不承順璋，璋殺魯母及弟，遂為讎敵。
units.en: Liu Zhang, courtesy Jiyu, inherited his father’s post. Zhang Lu grew insolent and defied him, so Liu Zhang executed Lu’s mother and brother, and the two became bitter enemies.
units.literal: Zhang, courtesy name Jiyu, having inherited Yan’s position, then Zhang Lu gradually became arrogant and self-indulgent, did not obey and comply with Zhang; Zhang killed Lu’s mother and younger brother; then they became enemy foes.

units.zh: 璋累遣龐羲等攻魯，數為所破。
units.en: Liu Zhang sent Pang Xi and others against Zhang Lu time and again, only to be routed repeatedly.
units.literal: Zhang repeatedly sent Pang Xi and others to attack Lu; several times were broken by him.

units.zh: 魯部曲多在巴西，故以羲為巴西太守，領兵禦魯。
units.en: Most of Zhang Lu’s followers were in Ba Commandery, so Liu Zhang named Pang Xi grand administrator there and put him on the northern front against Lu.
units.literal: Lu’s retainers were mostly in Ba Commandery; therefore Xi was made grand administrator of Ba Commandery, leading troops to resist Lu.

units.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：龐羲與璋有舊，又免璋諸子於難，故璋厚德羲，以羲為巴西太守，遂專權勢。〉
units.en: 〈The Record of Heroes notes: “Pang Xi was an old friend who had rescued Liu Zhang’s sons from peril, so Liu Zhang heaped favor on him, named him grand administrator of Ba, and let him dominate local power.”〉
units.literal: 〈The Record of Heroes says: Pang Xi had old ties with Zhang, moreover had saved Zhang’s various sons from disaster; therefore Zhang heavily favored Xi, made Xi grand administrator of Ba Commandery, and then he monopolized power and influence.〉

units.zh: 後羲與璋情好攜隙，趙韙稱兵內向，眾散見殺，皆由璋明斷少而外言入故也。
units.en: Later Pang Xi and Liu Zhang fell out; Zhao Wei turned his army on Chengdu, his troops melted away, and he was killed—all because Liu Zhang seldom judged matters for himself and let rumor rule his court.
units.literal: Later Xi and Zhang’s feelings and friendship carried a rift; Zhao Wei raised troops inward toward the capital; the host scattered and he was seen and killed; all was because Zhang had little clear decisive judgment and outside words entered.

units.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：先是，南陽、三輔人流入益州數万家，收以為兵，名曰東州兵。
units.en: 〈The Record of Heroes explains: Refugees from Nanyang and the Three Adjuncts had poured into Yizhou by the tens of thousands; Liu Zhang drafted them as the so-called Eastern Province host.
units.literal: 〈The Record of Heroes says: before this, people of Nanyang and the Three Adjuncts flowed into Yizhou in several tens of thousands of households; they were collected and made soldiers, named Eastern Province troops.

units.zh: 璋性寬柔，無威略，東州人侵暴舊民，璋不能禁，政令多闕，益州頗怨。
units.en: Liu Zhang was easygoing and lacked firm authority, so the easterners bullied the old families unchecked. Edicts went unenforced, and resentment spread through Yizhou.
units.literal: Zhang’s nature was lenient and soft; he had no awe-inspiring strategy; Eastern Province people violated and abused the old common people; Zhang could not prohibit it; government orders had many gaps; Yizhou was quite resentful.

units.zh: 趙韙素得人心，璋委任之。
units.en: Zhao Wei enjoyed wide popularity, and Liu Zhang leaned on him heavily.
units.literal: Zhao Wei always won people’s hearts; Zhang entrusted him.

units.zh: 韙因民怨謀叛，乃厚賂荊州請和，陰結州中大姓，與俱起兵，還擊璋。
units.en: Playing on popular anger, Zhao Wei plotted revolt: he bought a truce with Jingzhou in secret, won the great clans of the province, and marched on Chengdu against Liu Zhang.
units.literal: Wei because of the people’s resentment plotted rebellion; then he thickly bribed Jing Province to request peace, secretly bound the great surnames of the province, and together with them raised troops, turned back and attacked Zhang.

units.zh: 蜀郡、廣漢、犍為皆應韙。
units.en: Shu, Guanghan, and Qianwei all rose in his name.
units.literal: Shu, Guanghan, and Qianwei all responded to Wei.

units.zh: 璋馳入成都城守，東州人畏
units.en: Liu Zhang raced within Chengdu’s walls. The Eastern Province troops, fearing
units.literal: Zhang galloped into Chengdu city to defend it; men of the Eastern Province feared

units.en: disaster if the city fell (some editions insert the graph wei here),
units.literal: (wei ‘might’ [variant graph supplied in some editions]),

units.zh: 咸同心並力助璋，皆殊死戰，遂破反者，進攻韙於江州。
units.en: closed ranks behind Liu Zhang and fought to the last man. They shattered the rebels and drove the siege against Zhao Wei at Jiangzhou.
units.literal: all with one heart and combined strength aided Zhang; all fought to the death; then they broke the rebels and advanced to attack Wei at Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 韙將龐樂、李異反殺韙軍，斬韙。
units.en: Zhao Wei’s own generals Pang Le and Li Yi mutinied, cut down his troops, and took his head.
units.literal: Wei’s generals Pang Le and Li Yi turned mutinous, killed Wei’s army, and beheaded Wei.

units.zh: 《漢獻帝春秋》曰：漢朝聞益州亂，遣五官中郎將牛亶為益州刺史；
units.en: The Annals of Emperor Xian records: Learning of the turmoil, the court dispatched Niu Dan, general of the household for all purposes, as inspector of Yizhou;
units.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian of Han says: the Han court heard that Yizhou was in chaos and sent General of the Household for All Purposes Niu Dan as inspector of Yizhou;

units.zh: 徵璋為卿，不至。〉
units.en: it also summoned Liu Zhang to a ministerial post—which he ignored.
units.literal: summoned Zhang to be a minister; he did not arrive.

units.zh: 璋聞曹公徵荊州，已定漢中，遣河內陰溥致敬於曹公。
units.en: When Liu Zhang learned that Cao Cao was moving on Jingzhou and had already taken Hanzhong, he sent Yin Pu of Henei with gifts to court Cao’s favor.
units.literal: Zhang heard that Lord Cao was campaigning against Jing Province and had already pacified Hanzhong; he sent Yin Pu of Henei to present respects to Lord Cao.

units.zh: 加璋振威將軍，兄瑁平寇將軍。
units.en: The court added the title general who shakes might to Liu Zhang and named his elder brother Liu Mao general who pacifies bandits.
units.literal: Zhang was additionally given General Who Shakes Might; his elder brother Mao was given General Who Pacifies Bandits.

units.zh: 瑁狂疾物故。
units.en: Liu Mao died of madness.
units.literal: Mao of mad illness passed away (wu gu).

units.zh: 〈臣松之案：魏台訪「物故」之義，高堂隆答曰：「聞之先師：物，無也；
units.en: 〈Pei Songzhi cites the Wei court’s query on the term wu gu (“passed away”). Gao Tanglong replied: “My teacher explained: wu means ‘nothing’;
units.literal: 〈Pei Songzhi’s note: the Wei court inquired into the meaning of wu gu; Gao Tanglong answered saying: “I heard it from my former teacher: wu means ‘not’;

units.zh: 故，事也；
units.en: gu means ‘affair’;
units.literal: gu means ‘affair’;

units.zh: 言無復所能於事也。」〉
units.en: that is, no longer able to act in the world.””〉"
units.literal: it means saying one has no longer any capacity in affairs.”〉"

units.zh: 璋復遣別駕從事蜀郡張肅送叟兵三百人並雜御物於曹公，曹公拜肅為廣漢太守。
units.en: Liu Zhang next dispatched chief clerk Zhang Su of Shu with three hundred veteran troops and assorted tribute. Cao Cao rewarded him with the grand administrator’s seal of Guanghan.
units.literal: Zhang again sent chief clerk Zhang Su of Shu Commandery to deliver three hundred Sou troops together with miscellaneous imperial goods to Lord Cao; Lord Cao appointed Su grand administrator of Guanghan.

units.zh: 璋復遣別駕張松詣曹公，曹公時已定荊州，走先主，不復存錄松，松以此怨。
units.en: He then sent chief clerk Zhang Song. By then Cao Cao had overrun Jingzhou and routed Liu Bei; he treated Zhang Song with cold neglect, and Song nursed a grudge.
units.literal: Zhang again sent chief clerk Zhang Song to visit Lord Cao; Lord Cao at that time had already pacified Jing Province and driven away the Former Lord; he no longer kept record of Song; Song for this reason resented.

units.zh: 會曹公軍不利於赤壁，兼以疫死。
units.en: Then came Cao Cao’s defeat at Red Cliffs and the epidemic that decimated his army.
units.literal: It happened that Lord Cao’s army was not victorious at Red Cliffs, and moreover because of plague died.

units.zh: 松還，疵毀曹公，勸璋自絕，
units.en: Zhang Song returned to paint Cao Cao in the worst colors and urge Liu Zhang to break with the north,
units.literal: Song returned, faulted and slandered Lord Cao, urged Zhang to break off by himself,

units.zh: 〈《漢書春秋》曰：張松見曹公，曹公方自矜伐，不存錄松。
units.en: 〈The Springs and Autumns of the Han Book records: Zhang Song found Cao Cao swollen with pride over his victories and dismissive of him.
units.literal: 〈The Springs and Autumns of the Han Book says: Zhang Song met Lord Cao; Lord Cao was just then boasting of his achievements and did not keep record of Song.

units.zh: 松歸，乃勸璋自絕。
units.en: On his return he pressed Liu Zhang to cut ties with Cao Cao.
units.literal: Song returned, then urged Zhang to break off by himself.

units.zh: 習鑿齒曰：昔齊桓一矜其功而叛者九國，曹操暫自驕伐而天下三分，皆勤之於數十年之內而棄之於俯仰之頃，豈不惜乎！
units.en: Xi Zuochi comments: Duke Huan’s single burst of vanity cost him nine allies; Cao Cao’s moment of swagger cost him the unity of the empire. Decades of toil undone in an instant—could anything be more wasteful?
units.literal: Xi Zuochi said: in the past Duke Huan of Qi once prided himself on his merit and nine states rebelled; Cao Cao for a short time was arrogant and boastful and the realm split into three parts; all were toiled over within several tens of years and discarded in the space of a nod and a blink—how is it not regrettable!

units.zh: 是以君子勞謙日昃，慮以下人，功高而居之以讓，勢尊而守之以卑。
units.en: Hence the gentleman works tirelessly yet stays humble, thinks downward toward those below him, holds great merit with deference, and wields supreme power meekly.
units.literal: Therefore the gentleman toils in humility at sunset, considers so as to place himself below others, merit is high yet he occupies it with yielding, power is honored yet he guards it with lowliness.

units.zh: 情近於物，故雖貴而人不厭其重；
units.en: Staying close to the human condition, he can bear rank without wearying the world;
units.literal: Feeling draws near to things; therefore although noble yet people do not tire of his weight;

units.zh: 德洽群生，故業廣而天下愈欣其慶。
units.en: where virtue touches every life, his sway widens and the realm rejoices in his fortune.
units.literal: virtue harmonizes the mass of living beings; therefore the enterprise is broad and the realm ever more rejoices in his blessings.

units.zh: 夫然，故能有其富貴，保其功業，隆顯當時，傳福百世，何驕矜之有哉！
units.en: Only so can wealth and titles be sustained, achievement preserved, glory fixed in one’s own age, and blessings passed down for generations—where then is room for arrogance?
units.literal: Being thus, therefore he is able to have his wealth and honor, preserve his merit and enterprise, be illustrious in his time, transmit blessing a hundred generations—what arrogance and self-conceit is there!

units.zh: 君子是以知曹操之不能遂兼天下者也。〉
units.en: From this the gentleman sees why Cao Cao could never finish the conquest of the realm.
units.literal: The gentleman by this knows that Cao Cao could not in the end annex the whole realm.

units.zh: 因說璋曰：「劉豫州，使君之肺腑，可與交通。」
units.en: He went on to tell Liu Zhang: “Liu Bei of Yu Province is your own flesh and blood politically—you should open relations with him.”
units.literal: Thereupon he persuaded Zhang saying: “Lord Liu of Yu Province is your excellency’s inner liver and lungs; it is possible to communicate and connect with him.”

units.zh: 璋皆然之，遣法正連好先主，尋又令正及孟達送兵數千助先主守禦，正遂還。
units.en: Liu Zhang agreed, sent Fa Zheng to treat with Liu Bei, and shortly had Fa Zheng and Meng Da deliver several thousand soldiers to stiffen Liu Bei’s line. Fa Zheng then came home.
units.literal: Zhang all approved it; he sent Fa Zheng to connect friendship with the Former Lord; soon he also ordered Zheng and Meng Da to deliver several thousand troops to aid the Former Lord in guarding and defending; Zheng then returned.

units.zh: 後松復說璋曰：「今州中諸將龐羲、李異等皆恃功驕豪，欲有外意，不得豫州，則敵攻其外，民攻其內，必敗之道也。」
units.en: Later Zhang Song warned him again: “Pang Xi, Li Yi, and the other generals swagger on old laurels and eye independence. Without Liu Bei to stiffen your front, enemies will strike from without and your own people from within—that is the road to ruin.”
units.literal: Later Song again persuaded Zhang saying: “Now the various generals of the province such as Pang Xi and Li Yi all rely on merit and are arrogant and bold, wishing to have outward intentions; if you do not obtain Lord Liu of Yu Province, then enemies will attack from without and the people will attack from within—it is the way of certain defeat.”

units.zh: 璋又從之，遣法正請先主。
units.en: Liu Zhang consented again and sent Fa Zheng to invite Liu Bei in.
units.literal: Zhang again followed it; he sent Fa Zheng to invite the Former Lord.

units.zh: 璋主簿黃權陳其利害，從事廣漢王累自倒縣於州門以諫，璋一無所納，敕在所供奉先主，先主入境如歸。
units.en: Registrar Huang Quan laid out the risks; Wang Lei of Guanghan hanged himself upside down at the gate of the yamen in protest. Liu Zhang brushed every warning aside, ordered the route provisioned, and Liu Bei crossed the border as though coming home.
units.literal: Zhang’s registrar Huang Quan set forth its benefits and harms; clerk Wang Lei of Guanghan hung himself inverted at the province gate to remonstrate; Zhang accepted none of it; he ordered the places passed through to supply the Former Lord; the Former Lord entered the territory as if returning home.

units.zh: 先主至江州北，由墊江水
units.en: North of Jiangzhou, Liu Bei turned up the Dian River
units.literal: The Former Lord reached north of Jiangzhou, by the Dianjiang River’s waters

units.zh: 〈墊音徒協反。〉
units.en: Commentary: “Dian” is read like tu in the entering tone (dié).〉
units.literal: 〈Dian is read tu xie fan [phonetic].〉

units.zh: 詣涪，
units.en: He went on to Fu,
units.literal: went to Fu,

units.zh: 〈音浮。〉
units.en: 〈gloss: read like fú.〉
units.literal: 〈Sound fu.〉

units.zh: 去成都三百六十里，是歲建安十六年也。
units.en: He halted three hundred sixty li short of Chengdu, in the sixteenth year of Jian’an.
units.literal: It was three hundred sixty li from Chengdu; this year was the sixteenth year of Jian’an.

units.zh: 璋率步騎三萬馀人，車乘帳幔，精光曜日，往就與會；
units.en: Liu Zhang rode out with thirty thousand foot and horse, chariots draped in silk that flashed like sunlight, to meet him in person;
units.literal: Zhang led infantry and cavalry of more than thirty thousand men; chariots, carriages, tents, and curtains; refined brilliance dazzling the sun; went forward to join and meet him;

units.zh: 先主所將將士，更相之適，歡飲百馀日。
units.en: and for more than a hundred days Liu Bei’s officers and Liu Zhang’s hosts feasted together in easy camaraderie.
units.literal: The Former Lord’s led generals and soldiers, mutually exchanged courtesies and went back and forth, joyfully drank more than a hundred days.

units.zh: 璋資給先主，使討張魯，然後分別。
units.en: Liu Zhang provisioned Liu Bei and sent him to campaign against Zhang Lu, expecting afterward to go their separate ways.
units.literal: Zhang supplied and gave to the Former Lord, made him attack Zhang Lu, afterward to separate respectively.

units.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：璋以米二十萬斛，騎千匹，車千乘，繒絮錦帛，以資送劉備。〉
units.en: 〈The Book of Wu records that Liu Zhang sent Liu Bei two hundred thousand hu of grain, a thousand mounts, a thousand wagons, and bales of silk and brocade.〉
units.literal: 〈The Book of Wu says: Zhang used two hundred thousand hu of rice, one thousand horses, one thousand chariots, silk floss, brocade, and silks, thereby to supply and send Liu Bei.〉

units.zh: 明年，先主至葭萌，還兵南向，所在皆克。
units.en: The next year Liu Bei reached Jiameng, then wheeled his army south; every place he struck fell to him.
units.literal: The next year, the Former Lord reached Jiameng, turned the army southward, everywhere all were overcome.

units.zh: 十九年，進圍成都數十日，城中尚有精兵三萬人，谷帛支一年，吏民咸欲死戰。
units.en: In the nineteenth year of Jian’an he pressed a siege on Chengdu for many days. The city still held thirty thousand picked troops and grain and cloth enough for a year, and officials and townspeople were ready to fight to the last.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year, he advanced and besieged Chengdu several tens of days; inside the city there still were crack troops thirty thousand men, grain and silks sufficient for one year; officials and common people all wished to fight to the death.

units.zh: 璋言：「父子在州二十馀年，無恩德以加百姓。
units.en: Liu Zhang said, “My father and I have held this province for more than twenty years, yet we have done little real good for the people.
units.literal: Zhang said: “Father and son have been in the province more than twenty years; there is no kindness and virtue whereby to add to the common people.

units.zh: 百姓攻戰三年，肌膏草野者，以璋故也，何心能安！」
units.en: For three years they have borne our wars; their bones lie on the fields—for my sake. How could I live with myself in comfort?”
units.literal: The common people have attacked and fought three years; those whose flesh and fat grease the grasslands—because of Zhang; what heart can be at peace!”

units.zh: 遂開城出降，群下莫不流涕。
units.en: He opened the gates and surrendered; every man in his train wept.
units.literal: Then he opened the city and went out to surrender; among his subordinates none did not shed tears.

units.zh: 先主遷璋於南郡公安，盡歸其財物及故佩振威將軍印綬。
units.en: Liu Bei resettled Liu Zhang at Gong’an in Nan commandery and returned all his goods, together with the old seal and ribbon of the general who shakes might.
units.literal: The Former Lord relocated Zhang to Gongan in Nan Commandery; wholly returned his goods and property and his formerly worn seals and ribbons of General Who Shakes Might.

units.zh: 孫權殺關羽，取荊州，以璋為益州牧，駐秭歸。
units.en: After Sun Quan killed Guan Yu and seized Jingzhou, he named Liu Zhang governor of Yizhou and stationed him at Zigui.
units.literal: Sun Quan killed Guan Yu, took Jing Province, made Zhang governor of Yizhou, garrisoned Zigui.

units.zh: 璋卒，南中豪率雍闓據益郡反，附於吳。
units.en: When Liu Zhang died, the southern magnate Yong Kai seized Yi commandery in revolt and pledged himself to Wu.
units.literal: Zhang died; in the south magnate leader Yong Kai occupied Yi commandery and rebelled, attached to Wu.

units.zh: 權復以璋子闡為益州刺史，處交、益界首。
units.en: Sun Quan then appointed Liu Zhang’s son Liu Chan inspector of Yizhou and posted him on the Jiao–Yi frontier.
units.literal: Quan again used Zhang’s son Chan as inspector of Yizhou, placing him at the border head of Jiao and Yi.

units.zh: 丞相諸葛亮平南土，闡還吳，為御史中丞。
units.en: After Chancellor Zhuge Liang pacified the south, Liu Chan returned to Wu and was promoted to palace assistant censor-in-chief.
units.literal: Chancellor Zhuge Liang pacified the southern lands; Chan returned to Wu, became palace assistant censor-in-chief.

units.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：闡一名緯，為人恭恪，輕財愛義，有仁讓之風，後疾終於家。〉
units.en: 〈The Book of Wu adds that Liu Chan was also called Liu Wei: a courteous man who prized honor over money and died of illness at home.〉
units.literal: 〈The Book of Wu says: Chan had another name Wei; as a person he was respectful and careful, lightened wealth and loved righteousness, had the air of benevolence and yielding; later he died of illness at home.〉

units.zh: 初，璋長子循妻，龐羲女也。
units.en: Earlier, Liu Zhang’s eldest son Liu Xun had married a daughter of Pang Xi.
units.literal: At the beginning, Zhang’s eldest son Xun’s wife was Pang Xi’s daughter.

units.zh: 先主定蜀，羲為左將軍司馬，璋時從羲啟留循，先主以為奉車中郎將。
units.en: After Liu Bei conquered Shu, Pang Xi served as major to the general of the left. Liu Zhang at that time followed Pang Xi's petition to keep Liu Xun, and Liu Bei then commissioned Liu Xun as gentleman of the household for the chariot.
units.literal: The Former Lord pacified Shu; Xi was major to the General of the Left; Zhang at that time followed Xi’s memorial to detain Xun; the Former Lord made him gentleman of the household for the chariot.

units.zh: 是以璋二子之後，分在吳、蜀。
units.en: Thus the two sons of Liu Zhang afterward lived out their lives apart, one in Wu and one in Shu.
units.literal: Therefore as for the two sons of Zhang afterward, they were divided between Wu and Shu.

units.en: 【Appraisal】
units.literal: 【Appraisal heading】

units.zh: 評曰：昔魏豹聞許負之言則納薄姬於室，
units.en: The historian’s judgment runs: Long ago Wei Bao listened to the soothsayer Xu Fu and welcomed Lady Bo into his harem,
units.literal: The appraisal says: Formerly Wei Bao heard Xu Fu’s words then took concubine Bo Ji into the chamber,

units.zh: 〈孔衍《漢魏春秋》曰：許負，河內溫縣之婦人，漢高祖封為明雌亭侯。
units.en: 〈Kong Yan’s Springs and Autumns of Han and Wei identifies Xu Fu as a woman of Wen county in Henei whom Han Gaozu supposedly ennobled as mistress of Mingci village.
units.literal: 〈Kong Yan’s Springs and Autumns of Han and Wei says: Xu Fu was a woman of Wen County in Henei; Han Gaozu enfeoffed her as village mistress of Mingci.

units.zh: 臣松之以為今東人呼母為負，衍以許負為婦人，如為有似，然漢高祖時封皆列侯，未有鄉亭之爵，疑此封為不然。〉
units.en: Pei Songzhi notes that eastern dialects used fu for “mother,” which may explain Kong Yan’s treating Xu Fu as a woman—yet Gaozu’s reign ennobled only full marquises, never mere village titles, so that fief is almost certainly wrong.
units.literal: Your subject Songzhi considers that today eastern people call mother fu; Yan taking Xu Fu as a woman—if so there is resemblance; yet at Han Gaozu’s time enfeoffments were all full marquises, there were not village-hamlet ranks; I suspect this enfeoffment is incorrect.

units.zh: 劉歆見圖讖之文則名字改易，終於不免其身，而慶鍾二主。
units.en: Liu Xin changed his name after reading prognosticating texts, yet could not save himself, while the omen’s fulfillment fell instead upon two other sovereigns.
units.literal: Liu Xin saw the texts of charts and prophecies then changed names and characters; in the end did not escape his own person, yet the auspice concentrated on two lords.

units.zh: 此則神明不可虛要，天命不可妄冀，必然之驗也。
units.en: So it is: the spirits cannot be coaxed with empty prayers, and the mandate of Heaven cannot be forced—that is the hard lesson of their fates.
units.literal: This then is that the gods and numina cannot be emptily demanded; Heaven’s mandate cannot be recklessly hoped for—it is verification of necessity.

units.zh: 而劉焉聞董扶之辭則心存益土，聽相者之言則求婚吳氏，遽造輿服，圖竊神器，其惑甚矣。
units.en: Liu Yan took Dong Fu’s talk to heart and fixed his ambition on Yizhou, listened to a physiognomist and wed the Wu family, rushed out imperial-style carriages and robes, and angled for the throne—folly in its purest form.
units.literal: But Liu Yan heard Dong Fu’s phrases then his heart lodged in Yi soil; heard the physiognomist’s words then sought marriage with the Wu clan; hastily made carriage and apparel, plotted to steal the sacred vessels—his delusion was extreme.

units.zh: 璋才非人雄，而據土亂世，負乘致寇，自然之理，其見奪取，非不幸也。
units.en: Liu Zhang was no champion of men, yet he clutched a rich province in an age of chaos—a lesser man in a high carriage invites robbers by nature. That he lost his domain was less misfortune than inevitability.
units.literal: Zhang’s talents were not those of a human hero, yet he occupied territory in a chaotic age; bearing while riding brings bandits—it is natural principle; his being seen seized and taken is not misfortune.

units.zh: 〈張璠曰：劉璋愚弱而守善言，斯亦宋襄公、徐偃王之徒，未為無道之主也。
units.en: 〈Zhang Fan remarks: “Liu Zhang was dull and pliant yet clung to fine phrases—much like Duke Xiang of Song or King Yan of Xu; he hardly ranks among the truly lawless rulers.”
units.literal: 〈Zhang Fan says: Liu Zhang was foolish and weak yet preserved good words; this also is of the class of Duke Xiang of Song, King Yan of Xu—not to be deemed a lord without the Way.

units.zh: 張松、法正，雖有君臣之義不正，然固以委名附質，進不顯陳事勢，若韓嵩、
units.en: Zhang Song and Fa Zheng broke the bond between lord and vassal, yet they had formally pledged themselves: they did not lay the strategic facts plainly before their master, as did Han Song,
units.literal: Zhang Song, Fa Zheng—although the righteousness between ruler and minister was not correct, yet firmly they entrusted name and attached substance; advancing they did not openly set forth the situation of affairs, like Han Song,

units.zh: （劉光）
units.en: (Liu Guang)
units.literal: (Liu Guang)

units.zh: 劉先之說劉表，退不告絕奔亡，若陳平、韓信之去項羽，而兩端攜貳，為謀不忠，罪之次也。〉
units.en: 〔Liu Xian〕 in counseling Liu Biao, or on retreating failed to announce a clean break before fleeing, as Chen Ping and Han Xin had done when they left Xiang Yu—yet they played both sides; such disloyal scheming is the lesser crime.
units.literal: 〔Liu Xian〕’s persuading Liu Biao; withdrawing did not declare break and flee, like Chen Ping and Han Xin’s leaving Xiang Yu—yet wavering two ends, as planning not loyal, is the next grade of guilt.
